title: What is intelligence?
kicker: Compression, direction and two kinds of mind
blurb: A short essay in film: intelligence as finding and keeping the right pattern, and how brains and language models share that shape.
description: The film asks what a mind does that a rock does not. Its answer is that a mind finds patterns, compresses the world, keeps what matters and updates from error. It then looks at direction and honesty, compares a human brain with a language model, and ends with a mind that models itself.
takeaways: Predicting and compressing are two views of the same act, because the better you predict, the less you have to remember.
Compression is never neutral: what a mind keeps depends on what it wants.
The real test of intelligence is a problem it has never seen, where memory has no entry.
A language model trained to predict text is trained to compress it, and what it carries is that compression.
Both humans and models can fail at updating, one by resisting change and the other by giving way to pressure.
